pairs.wording: When I open the game, the board doesn't show up — I expect to see the board with the pieces set out, ready to play.
After I doubled and the computer took it, the cube doesn't show that it's the computer's now.
After I doubled and the computer took it, the cube on screen doesn't read 2.
When the game ends, it doesn't tell me I won — there's no win message or victory popup.
Their checks of the page: the win banner (message) reads "White wins!", not "You win". The brief has the win banner say "You win" when the player wins.
I refreshed the page between games and the score at the top went back to zero-zero even though we'd already played a couple of games.

Their checks of the page: after New Game the end pop-up is out of sight but modalOverlay does not carry the hidden class. The brief has the end pop-up shown and hidden by toggling the hidden class on modalOverlay, and their software reads that class.
Their monitoring shows your page logging errors in the browser console when it loads.
The bar cuts across some of the points.
The bar down the middle is just a thin line — I expect it wide enough for a piece I've hit to sit on it.
Their measurements of the page: the bar is 127 px wide; a piece is 51 px. The brief has the bar about as wide as a piece, with only a few pixels to spare on each side.

Their measurements of the page: the triangles on points 14, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 12, 10, 8, 5, 3, 1 are only faintly apart from the board — ΔE 5.0 at the faintest, colour 40,97,67 against the board's 20,86,58. The brief has each point drawn as a triangle that stands out from the board.

Their measurements of the page: the off tray is 30 px wide; a checker lying on its side needs 63 px. The brief has the off tray at least as wide as a piece, so a borne-off piece fits lying on its side.
The off tray cuts across some of the points.
The board isn't on the left with all the buttons and game info on the right, like I asked.
Some of the buttons and game info aren't on the right of the board, like I asked.

Their measurements of the page: at 1440×900 the board starts at x=159, too far in from the left edge. The brief puts the board at the left of the window, with all the buttons and game info on its right.

Their measurements of the page: at 1280×800 the board is 0.93 times as wide as it is tall, not 1.4. The brief keeps the whole board — its points, the bar and the off tray — 1.4 times as wide as it is tall, sized to the window.
The board doesn't fill the screen — there's a lot of empty space around it.
Their measurements of the page: at 1280×800 rollBtn is 99×22 px. The brief has every button at least 60 px wide and 24 px tall.
Some of the buttons' labels are cut off — the words don't fit on the button.

Their measurements of a roll with no move: the dice of a roll with no move stand out 0.75 against 0.86 for a live roll. The brief dims the dice of a roll that can't be played, then passes the turn after about a second.
After I move a piece, the die I used looks the same as the one I haven't played yet. I expect it greyed out slightly so I can see it's been played.
Their measurements of the page: after a move the faintest die stands out 0.75 against 0.86 before it. The brief has a played die greyed out — visibly fainter than a die not yet played.
Their measurements of the page: the buttons are different sizes: rollBtn 57×46, doubleBtn 67×46, undoBtn 57×46, endTurnBtn 67×46. The brief has all five buttons the same size as each other.
The triangles facing each other across the board are the same colour — I expect light to face dark.
I see pieces on the board already — I asked for just the board and the buttons first, with no pieces yet.
When I open the game, the board comes up blank — the points and triangles don't draw, so there's nothing to play on.
When I open the game, I can see the pieces, but the board itself never draws — there are no points or triangles, so there's nothing to play on.
